newsitem.title: CHINA: FOCUS-HK stocks scale new heights, more gains seen.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-HK stocks scale new heights, more gains seen.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index scaled new heights on Wednesday as a rally in the property sector propelled the index through 16,000 points with enough momentum to carry it further in days ahead, analysts said.
The Hang Seng Index charged to a record high of 16,055.19 points before closing up 211.12 points, or 1.34 percent, at an all-time closing high of 15,983.18.
It was the first time the index had breached 16,000 points, which had been considered a resistance level.
"It can go all the way to 16,100 in the next few days," said Ricky Tam, senior research manager at Delta Asia Securities.
Turnover was HK$21.69 billion (US$2.8 billion) compared with HK$17.60 billion on Tuesday, with Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd the most active stock.
Shares in the property developer rose HK$2.75 to HK$80.75.
"It was the obvious thing to do," said SocGen-Crosby Securities trader Miles Remington of the move into the property sector. "Every sector has had its day."
The property sector has been out of favour since Hong Kong's July 1 return to Chinese rule when the territory's new government vowed to tackle spiralling real estate prices.

Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities, said investors were hoping that a recent slowdown in the buoyant property market would prevent the government imposing punitive measures against property speculators.
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority said this week that the government's intention to increase the supply of residential property had led to a cooling in the property market.
"For the medium term, the property developers have underperformed so much that I don't think the downside risk is too great," said So.
Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd surged HK$3.00 to HK$95.50 and Henderson Land Development Co Ltd rose HK$3.00 to HK$71.75.
Futures-related activity, ahead of Wednesday's expiry of the July Hang Seng Index contract, and warrant issues also boosted the market, brokers said.
July Hang Seng Index futures closed up 217 points at 15,967.
So said a strong tone to overseas markets should keep local shares prices firm on Thursday.
"The Hang Seng Index should be able to remain above 16,000 for some time unless the overseas markets come down sharply."
A drop in the U.S. long bond yield to 6.38 percent overnight, its lowest level in eight months, had spurred gains in Wall Street stocks on Tuesday and should boost the market further, brokers said.
"The interest rate environment is favourable. The Chinese economy is favourable," said South China Holdings vice chairman Howard Gorges. "There is no reason why it should go down."
But Remington said it was hard to see where the market could go from current levels.
"Sixteen thousand was the target which a lot of brokerage firms had set for this year. The question is, from here how much further can we go? All the sectors have performed."
Tam said there may be some profit-taking next week after HSBC Holdings Plc and Hang Seng Bank Ltd release interim earnings on Monday.
"The market may move lower next week," he said. ($1 = $HK7.74)
